details: The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) for July rose by a modest 0.1% monthly, with core CPI, excluding food and energy, climbing 0.2%. This tame inflation data may lead the Federal Reserve to maintain its current interest rate policy. Traders were awaiting this key inflation gauge, which influences expectations for US interest rates and broader risk sentiment.
title: US CPI Data Shows Tame Inflation, Potentially Influencing Fed Policy

details: The Federal Reserve has maintained its federal funds rate within the 5-5.25% range, prioritizing further progress in combating inflation before considering any rate reductions. While some economists anticipate potential rate cuts later in the year if inflation continues to cool, the Fed's cautious stance underscores its commitment to achieving its 2% inflation target.
sourceName: NBC News (via Facebook for live monetary policy announcement summary)
title: Federal Reserve Maintains Interest Rates Amid Inflation Vigilance

details: The ongoing standoff between the United States and Iran regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has kept oil prices elevated, with Brent trading around $89-$90 a barrel. This geopolitical tension and the resulting increase in oil prices are exacerbating inflation concerns, which could prompt central banks to maintain hawkish monetary policies to combat energy-driven inflation.
title: Rising Oil Prices and Geopolitical Tensions Fuel Inflation Concerns

details: The cryptocurrency market experienced a pullback on August 11, 2026, with Bitcoin (BTC) falling below $64,000 and the total crypto market capitalization decreasing by about 1.29% to $2.19 trillion. Ethereum (ETH) also saw declines. This downturn was largely attributed to broader market caution ahead of the US CPI data release, signaling a sensitivity to macroeconomic factors. Institutional Bitcoin ETF flows turned negative on August 10, with $144.6 million in net outflows, breaking a seven-day positive streak.
title: Crypto Market Pulls Back Ahead of US Inflation Data; ETF Flows Negative

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is scheduled to hold an open meeting on August 12, 2026, to discuss tailored rules for crypto asset investment contracts, a development that could significantly impact institutional participation and investor protections. Separately, Coinbase has obtained a Financial Services Permission (FSP) from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) to establish an international securities tokenization hub. This hub aims to conduct investment matching and custody for security tokens backed by underlying stocks.
title: SEC Meeting on Crypto Regulation & Coinbase's Global Expansion
